decision: Every pull request must be validated against the knowledge graph rules and checked for functionality the graph doesn't yet name.
why: Without automated validation, rule violations reach the codebase unchallenged and the graph stops describing what the code actually does.
steps: On pull_request opened or synchronize, check out the repo at the PR head with full history.
Collect the full diff (git diff origin/<base>...HEAD) and the full content of every non-deleted changed file. Cap total injected content at 50 KB; truncate with a note beyond that.

Run claude -p with the diff and file contents from the repo root so CLAUDE.md context loads automatically. Ask Claude to check every rule in all three layers - foundations, constitutive, regulative - and return a verdict for every single one, including rules that do not apply.

Ask Claude to separately identify any functionality, capability, or resource type the diff introduces that no vocabulary, constitutive, or regulative node names - regardless of whether it violates an existing rule.

Ask Claude to return JSON: {"result": "PASS"|"FAIL", "summary": {"what": "...", "why": "..."}, "foundations": [...], "constitutive": [...], "regulative": [...], "uncovered": [...]}, where uncovered holds one entry per gap found, each with a description of the new functionality and the evidence (file/line) that introduced it.

Parse the JSON output. Render each layer as a section: failed rules listed with violation and evidence, passed rules collapsed under a details toggle. Render uncovered findings as their own section. result is FAIL if any rule in any layer has status fail or uncovered contains one or more entries, and a FAIL result must fail the workflow job so GitHub Actions visibly reports advisory findings.
Post the formatted findings as a pull request comment, prefixed with the what/why summary and suffixed with model, token count, and cost in EUR.
violations: Validation configured as a required status check, blocking merge on findings.
graph.md included in the injected file content.
